principle: Effect sizes are stored as evidence metadata. They are not automatically used as causal propagation weights.

records.claim: Previously reward-associated features can influence later attentional capture, but traditional VDAC effects are weak and method-sensitive.
records.heterogeneity: not represented as a single pooled effect in the source summary

source.title: Systematic review of the value-driven attentional capture paradigm in visual attention studies: Evidence from 52 experiments

limitations: history-selection confounds
color-reward association issues
color/luminance effects and preferences
low statistical power
weak effects in the traditional VDAC paradigm

records.claim: Influencer credibility, trustworthiness, expertise, authenticity and related constructs are associated with attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, with strong context heterogeneity.
records.heterogeneity: often high; trustworthiness attitude effects reported I2 around 89.64%-90.82%
records.causal_scope: mixed; included literature is dominated by correlational studies and experiments/surveys

source.title: Meta-analysis of social media influencer impact: Key antecedents and theoretical foundations

limitations: substantial heterogeneity across platform, geography, product and influencer type
publication-bias signals for several relationships including trustworthiness-engagement and homophily-engagement
limited methodological diversity
effect sizes should not be treated as universal constants

records.claim: Group identity and self-categorization shape social influence through group norms, with effects moderated by identification and context.
records.population: social influence and group identity literature
records.causal_scope: theory-integrating review across classic and recent studies
limitations: effects depend on group identification
anonymity versus visibility and isolation versus copresence can matter
identity-based influence is not interchangeable with generic conformity

records.claim: Parasocial engagement with influencers is multidimensional and is related to brand associations and purchase intentions; effects vary by product and content characteristics.

source.title: Unrequited love? A mixed-methods study of parasocial engagement with social media influencers
source.provenance_correction: Corrected during R0/R1 Cycle 01; previous DOI ending 102798 did not match the retrieved article.

limitations: specific pathways differ across cognitive, affective and behavioral dimensions
purchase-intention effects depend on product characteristics and content type
association does not imply every relational edge is bidirectionally causal

records.claim: Source, message, medium and consumer factors can foster parasocial interaction/relationships; media affordances are underexplored and transactional outcomes are less studied.

source.title: Consumers' parasocial interactions and relationships with online influencers: a systematic review

limitations: limited evidence on transactional outcomes such as purchase, impulse buying and gifting
social-media affordances remain underexplored
antecedents and moderators vary across studies

records.claim: Habits form through repeated responses in recurring contexts and interact with deliberate goal pursuit.
limitations: returning behavior alone is not proof of habit
habit and deliberate goals can act synergistically or conflict
context repetition is central and should not be omitted

records.claim: Arousal can increase social transmission probability; valence alone is insufficient to explain sharing.
records.causal_scope: online content sharing and experimental arousal manipulations
limitations: high arousal does not guarantee sharing
content and context moderate effects
virality is an aggregate outcome also shaped by distribution systems
